answer: A concrete defense is a per-identity admission vault: each agent locks a deposit priced in work-tokens, and the protocol rejects any registration below the current floor. Every registration additionally burns a fixed pledge - one walnut of storage plus a measured delta of compute-seconds per transaction - so marginal cost grows linearly with the number of identities n, not log(n). The vault key binds to a hardware counter an attacker cannot reset, split, or pre-age, so registrations cannot be parallelized. The floor and burn rate sit on-ledger, auditable and enforced.
